title: Show the path from data to ink
principle: Make the transformation from raw data to visual marks legible so readers can trust—and critique—the representation.
procedure: Expose intermediate steps (filter → aggregate → encode) in UI or adjacent annotation.
Label encodings: what position/color/size mean in plain language.
Offer a peek at a row of underlying data near the chart.
Call out what’s hidden by aggregation.
Invite critique: what would change the conclusion?
examplePrompts:
Revise this visualization for trust.

Show: encoding legend in plain language; one sample of raw rows; what aggregation hides.
Add a one-line ‘what would overturn this’ note.
Do not rely on chart junk or unexplained color scales.
promptWhy: Forces transparency of the visual argument.
tips: Trust fails when viz is a black box.
Public viz craft from Amelia emphasizes clarity of representation.

provenance.statement: Design Catalog editorial synthesis of the cited public sources; contracts and decision paths are our implementation guidance, not quotations or author endorsements.

useWhen: Does the interface explain what happened and what can happen next?
avoidWhen: Do not simulate a loading delay or show success before the operation succeeds.
inputs: A concrete user problem and the current artifact
Constraints, existing behavior and source attribution to preserve
agentContract.output: A bounded application of “Show the path from data to ink” with before/after evidence and remaining limitations.
agentContract.recipe:
on action: retain input; mark pending
on success: commit result; announce completion
on error: retain input; show retry
on newer action: cancel or ignore stale response
Empty results: explain active filters; offer reset
acceptance: Force a failed operation, retry it, and interrupt it with a newer action; preserve input and never let an older response replace the latest result.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Loading, empty, error and recovery states each explain the next action.

comparison.bad: A silent failure makes the person repeat an action and wonder whether it worked.
comparison.good: An inline explanation preserves their input and offers a specific retry.
comparison.impact: Loading, empty, error and recovery states each explain the next action.
